sourceClaims.claim: All 40 named colors preserve source spelling, RGB value, and alpha.
Text, surface, border, action, and status roles are semantic aliases.
Component-local paints are retained when the source does not establish a global palette token.
WCAG observations do not rewrite the source-backed palette in Wave 1.

evidence.source-integrity: pass: source tests retain all 40 named paints, including 16 explicit alpha values, without rounding or opaque conversion
evidence.structural-contract: pass: all 11 semantic color aliases resolve to authored source paints and generated CSS contains no unresolved source alias
evidence.runtime-browser: pass: focused browser assertions verify primary, alpha, text, surface, and notification-shadow paint outcomes
evidence.accessibility: not-applicable: palette fidelity and representative paint application do not establish component contrast or WCAG compliance; those remain component and consumer audit claims
evidence.focused-visual: pass: representative currentColor and preserved-paint icon snapshots exercise source-backed paint topology without palette substitution
evidence.consumer-integration: pass: representative field, notification, icon, and Data Workspace surfaces consume published color variables or documented component-local source paints
evidence.responsive-content-stress: not-applicable: color claims do not change with viewport or content length
